newsitem.title: GERMANY: SGL Carbon sees long-term earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: SGL Carbon sees long-term earnings growth.

text.p: German carbon and graphite group SGL Carbon AG said on Monday it expected further long-term growth in earnings after posting a 35 percent rise in pre-tax profit in the first nine months of 1996.

"We see no reason to weaken our frequently stated forecast for a long-term positive growth trend for earnings," chief executive Robert Koehler said in a statement prepared for delivery at a news conference.
Koehler said that orders for graphite electrodes in particular made the company confident that demand for carbon and graphite products would pick up markedly in the final quarter.
Koehler said SGL therefore expected business to return to the positive performance seen in the first half of the year.
Group net profit rose to 140 million marks ($92.5 million) in the first nine months from 110 million marks while operating profit rose to 231 million marks from 186 million.
Group sales in the period rose to 1.285 billion marks from 1.172 billion.
